IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the brief: the MRT Jakarta East-West Line is NOT in passenger service. As of 2026-10-20 the only operating MRT line is the North-South Line Phase 1 (13 stations, 15.7 km). The official MRT Jakarta project page describes the East-West Line as 'Fase 1 Tahap 1' (Phase 1 Stage 1) = Tomang-Medan Satria, 24.5 km, with groundbreaking on 11 September 2024. 'Jakarta International Stadium' and 'Kota Intan' in the brief are LRT Jakarta / planned-LRT names, not MRT Jakarta East-West Line stations.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the brief: there is no MRT Jakarta 'Phase 1.5 (Bundaran HI - Ancol)'. The extension north of Bundaran HI is Phase 2A (7 underground stations: Thamrin, Monas, Harmoni, Sawah Besar, Mangga Besar, Glodok, Kota; segment 1 target 2027, segment 2 target 2029) followed by Phase 2B (Kota-Ancol Barat).

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the brief: LRT Jakarta is a single elevated line with 11 stations over 12.2 km (Kelapa Gading - Manggarai), not 13 stations over 5.1 km. The original 5.8 km / 6-station operation (Pegangsaan Dua/Kelapa Gading - Velodrome) has been in commercial service since 1 December 2019; the Phase 1B extension to Manggarai was inaugurated by President Prabowo Subianto on 16 September 2026.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the brief: LRT Jabodebek has 18 stations in Phase 1 (not 31), on two lines that share a common Dukuh Atas-Cawang trunk: Cibubur Line (Dukuh Atas-Harjamukti, 25.94 km) and Bekasi Line (Dukuh Atas-Jati Mulya, 29.54 km). Both opened on 28 August 2023. There is no 'Cawang-Depok Baru' or 'Cawang-Cibubur' branch pair.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the brief: the KRL 'Cibubur Line' is the former name of the Commuter Line Bogor. The KRL Lingkar (loop) route was reduced to five Jabodetabek lines after the 28 May 2022 restructuring. The Tanjung Priok Line runs Jakarta Kota - Kampung Bandan - Ancol - Jakarta International Stadium - Tanjung Priok.

Station codes: MRT Jakarta uses 3-letter codes (LBB, FTM, CPR, HJN, BLA, BLM, SSM, SNY, IST, BNH, STB, DKA, BHI). LRT Jakarta uses S-01..S-11 with 3-letter abbreviations. LRT Jabodebek uses 3-letter codes (DKA, SET, RAS, KUA, CKK, CIL, CWG, TMI, KAM, CRC, HAR, HAL, JBU, CK1, CK2, BEK, JTM). KAI uses 3-letter codes (JAKK, MGI, TPK, CW, ...). Indonesian Wikipedia additionally carries an 'NSnn' sequence for the MRT North-South Line and JakRSN badges (B/C/R/T/TP/A prefixes for KRL lines, M for MRT, S for LRT Jakarta, CB/BK for LRT Jabodebek, EW for the MRT East-West Line). Both are recorded in the note fields.

Coordinates are WGS84 decimal degrees taken from the Wikipedia infobox {{coord}} template where available, otherwise from the Wikidata P625 claim. Coordinates are null where no verifiable value could be found; no coordinate is estimated. Planned / not-yet-built stations (MRT Phase 2A/2B, MRT East-West Line) therefore have null coordinates.
No official GTFS feed was found for any of the four operators. See the report for every API endpoint that was tested.

The LRT Jakarta live-schedule API (https://lrtjakarta.co.id/api/schedule/live) and the LRT Jakarta /schedule page are the only machine-readable real-time endpoints found. They require no authentication.
